_about: Curated by hand from SEBI circular HO/24/13/15(2)2026-IMD-RAC4/I/5764/2026 dated 26 Feb 2026 (Categorisation and Rationalisation of MF Schemes). The daily GitHub Action does NOT edit this file; it only flags new SEBI circulars and any AMFI category label that doesn't match an 'amfi' alias below.

groups.name: Equity
groups.about: Invest mainly in company shares. Highest growth potential, biggest ups and downs. For money you won't need for 5+ years.

groups.name: Debt
groups.about: Lend money to governments, banks and companies for interest. Steadier, lower returns. For parking money and short to medium goals.

groups.name: Hybrid
groups.about: Mix shares, bonds and sometimes gold in one fund, so the ride is smoother than pure equity.

groups.name: Life Cycle
groups.about: Pick a target year. The fund starts growth-heavy and becomes safer by itself as the year approaches.

groups.name: Other
groups.about: Funds that copy an index, or funds that invest in other funds.

groups.name: Solution Oriented
groups.about: Retirement and children's funds. Closed to new investors since February 2026.

categories.name: Multi Cap Fund
categories.rule: At least 75% in shares, with at least 25% each in large, mid and small companies.
categories.what: Owns big, medium and small companies, with at least a quarter of the money in each size. It can't quietly drift into only big companies.
stat: each in large, mid and small
categories.clue: Must keep at least a quarter of its money in each of large, mid and small companies.

categories.name: Large Cap Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in large companies (India's top 100 by market value).
categories.what: Owns India's 100 biggest listed companies. The steadiest equity fund, but it can still fall 30% or more in a bad year.
categories.clue: At least 80% of its money is in India's 100 biggest companies.

categories.name: Large & Mid Cap Fund
categories.rule: At least 35% in large companies and at least 35% in mid-sized companies.
categories.what: Owns the 100 biggest companies plus the next 150, for more growth than a large cap fund with a bit more risk.
categories.clue: Must hold at least 35% in the top 100 companies and at least 35% in companies ranked 101 to 250.

categories.name: Mid Cap Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in mid-sized companies (ranked 101 to 250).
categories.what: Owns mostly medium-sized companies. More room to grow than big companies, and deeper falls in bad years.
categories.clue: At least 65% in companies ranked 101 to 250 by size.

categories.name: Small Cap Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in small companies (ranked 251 and below).
categories.what: Owns mostly smaller companies. The biggest growth potential and the wildest swings; it can stay down for years.
categories.clue: At least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by size.

categories.name: Flexi Cap Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in shares, any mix of company sizes.
categories.what: The fund manager is free to mix big, medium and small companies in any proportion and change it over time.
categories.clue: At least 65% in shares, with no minimum for any company size.

categories.name: Dividend Yield Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in shares of companies that pay dividends.
categories.what: Owns companies that pay regular dividends. It's still an equity fund: the dividends don't make it safe like a deposit.
categories.clue: At least 80% in companies known for paying regular dividends.

categories.name: Value Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in shares, picked with a value approach.
categories.what: Buys companies that look cheap compared with what they earn or own, and waits for the market to notice.
categories.clue: Hunts for shares priced below what the business seems to be worth.

categories.name: Contra Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in shares, picked by going against current market sentiment.
categories.what: Deliberately buys what most investors are avoiding right now, betting the crowd is wrong.
categories.clue: Deliberately buys what the crowd is selling or ignoring.

categories.name: Focused Fund
categories.rule: No more than 30 stocks; at least 80% in shares.
categories.what: Holds 30 companies or fewer, so each pick matters more, for better or worse.
categories.clue: Allowed to hold no more than 30 stocks.

categories.name: Sectoral Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in one sector, e.g. banking or healthcare.
categories.what: Invests in one industry only, like banking or pharma. It rises and falls with that industry.
categories.clue: Puts at least 80% of its money into a single industry, like banking or pharma.

categories.name: Thematic Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in one theme that can cover several sectors.
categories.what: Invests in one idea that spans several industries, like consumption or manufacturing. Narrower than a diversified fund.
categories.clue: Built around one idea, like rural consumption, that spans several industries.

categories.name: ELSS – Tax Saver Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in shares; each investment is locked for 3 years.
categories.what: An equity fund that saves tax under the old tax regime (Section 80C, up to Rs 1.5 lakh a year). Your money is locked for 3 years.
categories.clue: The only fund type with a 3-year lock-in that also gives a Section 80C tax deduction.

categories.name: Overnight Fund
categories.rule: Invests only in securities that mature the next day.
categories.horizon: a day to a few weeks
categories.what: Lends money for just one day at a time, mostly to banks against government bonds. Almost no risk, and returns to match.
categories.clue: Everything it owns matures by the next day.

categories.name: Liquid Fund
categories.rule: Invests only in debt that matures within 91 days.
categories.what: The usual home for an emergency fund or money needed within weeks. Low risk, and money usually reaches you the next working day.
categories.clue: Can't own anything that matures later than 91 days.

categories.name: Ultra Short Term Fund
categories.rule: Average duration of 3 to 6 months.
categories.what: For money you'll need in 3 to 6 months. A little more return than a liquid fund, still low risk.
categories.clue: Keeps its average duration between 3 and 6 months.

categories.name: Ultra Short to Short Term Fund
categories.rule: Average duration of 6 to 12 months.
categories.what: For money you'll need in 6 to 12 months.
amfi: Ultra Short to Short Term Fund
categories.clue: Keeps its average duration between 6 and 12 months.

categories.name: Money Market Fund
categories.rule: Invests only in money market instruments that mature within 1 year.
categories.what: Lends for up to a year through short-term instruments issued by banks, companies and the government.
categories.clue: Holds only short-term IOUs from banks, companies and the government that mature within a year.

categories.name: Short Term Fund
categories.rule: Average duration of 1 to 3 years.
categories.what: A common choice for goals 1 to 3 years away. High-quality lending with modest ups and downs.
categories.clue: Keeps its average duration between 1 and 3 years.

categories.name: Medium Term Fund
categories.rule: Average duration of 3 to 4 years (can be cut to 1 year if the manager expects trouble).
categories.what: Lends for a bit longer, so it moves more when interest rates change. Better for 3+ years.
categories.clue: Keeps its average duration between 3 and 4 years.

categories.name: Medium to Long Term Fund
categories.rule: Average duration of 4 to 7 years (can be cut to 1 year if the manager expects trouble).
categories.what: Lends for longer still. It gains when interest rates fall and loses when they rise.
categories.clue: Keeps its average duration between 4 and 7 years.

categories.name: Long Term Fund
categories.rule: Average duration of more than 7 years.
categories.what: Lends for the longest periods, so it's the most sensitive to interest rate changes of any debt fund.
categories.clue: Its average duration must be more than 7 years.

categories.name: Dynamic Term Fund
categories.rule: Any duration; the manager changes it with their view on rates.
categories.what: The manager lends for shorter or longer periods depending on where they think interest rates are heading.
categories.clue: Has no duration limit; the manager changes it based on their view of interest rates.

categories.name: Corporate Bond Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in bonds rated AA+ or higher.
categories.what: Lends to companies with the highest credit ratings, so the chance of not being repaid is low.
categories.clue: At least 80% in company bonds with the top credit ratings (AA+ or higher).

categories.name: Credit Risk Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in bonds rated AA or lower.
categories.what: Earns extra interest by lending to lower-rated companies, and takes on a real risk that some won't repay.
categories.clue: At least 65% in bonds rated below the top grades, for extra interest.

categories.name: Banking and PSU Debt Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in debt of banks, public sector companies and municipal bodies.
categories.what: Lends mainly to banks and government-owned companies. Low chance of default.
categories.clue: At least 80% lent to banks, government-owned companies and city bodies.

categories.name: Gilt Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in government securities.
categories.what: Lends only to the government, so there's no risk of not being repaid. Prices still move with interest rates.
categories.clue: At least 80% in government bonds, of any maturity.

categories.name: 10-year Constant Maturity Gilt Fund
categories.rule: At least 80% in government securities, with a 10-year duration.
categories.what: Lends to the government with its duration fixed at 10 years, so it moves closely with the 10-year government bond.
amfi: Gilt Fund with 10 year constant duration
Gilt Fund with 10 year Constant Duration
categories.clue: Holds government bonds with its duration fixed at 10 years.

categories.name: Floating Interest Rates Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in floating-rate instruments.
categories.what: Holds bonds whose interest rate resets with the market, so it holds up better when rates rise.
categories.clue: At least 65% in bonds whose interest rate resets with market rates.

categories.name: Sectoral Fund (Debt)
categories.rule: At least 80% in AA+ or higher rated bonds of one sector (financial services, energy, infrastructure, housing or real estate).
categories.what: New in 2026. Lends to top-rated borrowers in one sector, such as housing or energy, so trouble in that sector hits harder.
stat: in top-rated bonds of one sector
categories.clue: A debt fund that lends at least 80% to top-rated borrowers in a single sector like housing or energy.

categories.name: Conservative Hybrid Fund
categories.rule: 10–25% in shares, 75–90% in debt.
categories.what: Mostly debt with a small slice of shares (10–25%) for a bit of extra growth.
categories.clue: Keeps just 10 to 25% in shares and the rest in debt.

categories.name: Balanced Hybrid Fund
categories.rule: 40–60% in shares and 40–60% in debt; no arbitrage.
categories.what: A roughly even split between shares and debt.
categories.clue: Splits roughly half and half between shares and debt, with no arbitrage allowed.

categories.name: Aggressive Hybrid Fund
categories.rule: 65–80% in shares, 20–35% in debt.
categories.what: Mostly shares (65–80%) with a debt cushion. Taxed like an equity fund.
categories.clue: Keeps 65 to 80% in shares and the rest in debt.

categories.name: Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund
categories.was: Dynamic Asset Allocation or Balanced Advantage
categories.rule: The share and debt mix changes over time, usually following a model.
categories.what: Often called a Balanced Advantage Fund. It cuts shares when markets look expensive and adds when they look cheap, by itself.
amfi: Dynamic Asset Allocation or Balanced Advantage
Balanced Advantage Fund/ Dynamic Asset Allocation
categories.clue: Shifts between shares and debt by itself as markets look cheaper or dearer.

categories.name: Multi Asset Allocation Fund
categories.rule: At least 10% each in three or more asset classes.
categories.what: Holds at least three kinds of investment, usually shares, debt and gold or silver, in one fund.
categories.clue: Must hold at least 10% each in three or more kinds of assets.

categories.name: Arbitrage Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in shares, fully hedged; its debt is limited to short government securities.
categories.what: Earns the small price gap between the cash and futures markets. Low risk like a debt fund, but taxed like equity.
categories.clue: Earns the price gap between buying shares and selling their futures at the same time.

categories.name: Equity Savings Fund
categories.rule: At least 65% in shares, but only 15–40% exposed to market moves; at least 10% in debt.
categories.what: Mixes shares with protective trades that cancel out most market moves, plus debt. Only 15–40% really moves with the market, so the ride is smoother than equity.
categories.clue: Only 15 to 40% of its money actually moves with the stock market; the rest is hedged or in debt.

categories.name: Life Cycle Fund
categories.rule: Target date 5 to 30 years away in multiples of 5; follows a set path from shares to debt; exit load of 3%, 2% and 1% in years 1 to 3.
categories.what: New in 2026. Named after a target year, like 2045. It starts mostly in shares and moves to safer investments by itself as the year approaches.
categories.clue: Named after a target year and moves from shares to debt by itself as that year approaches.

categories.name: Index Funds / ETFs
categories.rule: At least 95% in the securities of the index it tracks.
categories.what: Copies an index, like the Nifty 50, instead of picking stocks. Very low cost. ETFs trade on the stock exchange and need a demat account.
categories.clue: Simply copies a market benchmark like the Nifty 50, with no stock-picking.

categories.name: Fund of Funds (Domestic & Overseas)
categories.rule: At least 95% in its underlying fund or funds.
categories.what: A fund that invests in other funds, for example to reach foreign markets or combine a few funds in one.
categories.clue: Puts at least 95% of its money into other mutual funds.

categories.name: Retirement Fund
categories.rule: Locked in for 5 years or until retirement age, whichever is earlier.
categories.what: Closed to new investors since February 2026. Existing investments continue until they're merged into similar funds.

categories.name: Children's Fund
categories.rule: Locked in for 5 years or until the child turns 18, whichever is earlier.
categories.what: Closed to new investors since February 2026. Existing investments continue until they're merged into similar funds.

otherTypes.group: How you can buy and sell

items.name: Open-ended fund
items.text: Buy or sell any working day at that day's NAV. Almost every fund you'll see is open-ended.

items.name: Close-ended fund
items.text: You can invest only when it launches (the NFO) and it runs for a fixed term. To exit early you must sell on the stock exchange, often below NAV.

items.name: Interval fund
items.text: Lets you buy or sell only on set dates, e.g. once a quarter.

items.name: Active fund
items.text: A fund manager chooses what to buy, aiming to beat an index. Costs more.

items.name: Passive fund
items.text: Index funds and ETFs simply copy an index like the Nifty 50. Costs much less; you get the market's return.

items.name: ETF (Exchange Traded Fund)
items.text: A passive fund you buy and sell on the stock exchange like a share. Needs a demat account.

items.name: Gold and silver ETFs
items.text: Track the price of gold or silver without you storing any metal.

items.name: Target Maturity Fund
items.text: A debt index fund that matures on a fixed date, a bit like a fixed deposit that's traded daily.

items.name: Fixed Maturity Plan (FMP)
items.text: A close-ended debt fund held to a fixed date. Returns are more predictable but not guaranteed.

items.name: ESG fund
items.text: Invests in companies screened for environmental, social and governance standards.

items.name: Smart beta fund
items.text: An index fund whose index is built on a rule other than company size, e.g. equal weights or low volatility.

items.name: Specialised Investment Fund (SIF)
items.text: A newer product between mutual funds and portfolio management, with a minimum of Rs 10 lakh. Not for beginners.
